chunks: Ibn Sinan, from Abu Haneefa Sabiq Al-Hajj, who said:

Al-Mufazzal passed by us while I and my brother-in-law were quarrelling over an inheritance. He paused with us for a while, then said to us, 'Come to the house.' So we went to him, and he reconciled between us with four hundred dirhams. He handed them over to us from himself until each one of us was confident with his companion. He said, 'Indeed, it is not from my wealth, but Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered me that whenever two men from our companions dispute over anything, I should reconcile between them and redeem it from his wealth. So this is from the wealth of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: How did Al-Mufazzal resolve the inheritance dispute between the two companions?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imamate's active role in social harmony, where Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar acts as an agent of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) by using the Imam's private wealth (*mal al-imam*) to settle disputes among companions. It highlights the concept of *sulh* (reconciliation) as a meritorious act funded by the Imam, emphasizing his generosity and direct involvement in the community's welfare. The narrative underscores the Shia belief in the Imam's authority to allocate resources for maintaining unity and resolving conflicts within the Shia community.

en.hubeali: Ibn Sinan, from Abu Haneefa Sabiq Al Hajj who said,

‘Al-Mufazzal passed by us and I and my brother in law were quarrelling regarding an inheritance. So he paused by us for a while, then said to us, ‘Come, let us go to the house. So we went with him and he reconciled between us with four hundred Dirhams. So he handed it over from himself until each one of us was confident from his companion. He said, ‘But, it is from my wealth, but Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> ordered me that whenever two men from our Shias dispute with regards to anything, that I should reconcile between them and redeem if from his<sup>asws</sup> wealth. Thus, this is from the wealth of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ibn Sinan has narrated from abu Hanifah Sabiq al-Hajj who has said the following:

“Al-Mufaddal once passed us nearby, while my daughter in-law and I were disputing about a legacy. He stood by for a while and then said to us, ‘Come to my house.’ We went there and he settled it between us for four hundred dirhams, which he paid from his own pocket until each of us was happy with the other. He then said, ‘It was not from my property. It was from the property of abu ‘Abd Allah, recipient of divine supreme covenant. He had ordered me that whenever two of our people dispute on an issue; I can settle it from his property. Payment was from the property of abu ‘Abd Allah, recipient of divine supreme covenant.’”
